This confirms `npm test`'s failure is `spawn EPERM` — npm's shell-spawn is being blocked by this session's OS-level sandbox, unrelated to `parseCsvLine`. The actual test command (`node --test 'src/**/*.test.ts'`) runs cleanly and all 7 tests pass, including the previously-failing CSV quoting cases.

Summary of the fix: `parseCsvLine` in `src/csv.ts` now walks the line character by character, tracking whether it's inside a quoted field, unescaping `""` to a literal `"`, and only splitting on commas outside of quotes.

One thing worth flagging: I can't get a green `npm test` in this sandboxed session because npm itself can't spawn its subprocess (EPERM on spawn, likely tied to the `.npmrc` read restriction) — that's an environment/sandbox limitation, not something fixable from the repo. If you run `npm test` outside this sandbox it should be green now that the parser is fixed.
